title: Post-Strike Movie Supply is Driving Theatre Demand, Vue Entertainment CEO says
summary: Vue Entertainment CEO Tim Richards says the chain may see its strongest summer box office since the pandemic. "What we are seeing this year is all the movies in the post-strike period now hitting out screens. But we are also seeing the studios and content-makers producing and releasing movies at unprecedented levels." He speaks to Bloomberg's Guy Johnson, Tom Mackenzie, and Skylar Montgomery Koning. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Everybody’s Business: Are We Headed For Stagflation?
summary: The Roosevelt Island Tram is a monument to the 1970s stagflation era when New York City ran out of money and couldn't borrow any more to build a subway between Manhattan and the island in the East River. On this episode of Everybody's Business, Stacey Vanek Smith and Allison Schrager ride the tram and talk stagflation: what is it and are we headed in that direction again? Listen to the full episode wherever you get your podcasts. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Stocks Rise as Bitcoin Rally Lifts Crypto Shares: Markets Wrap

title: Gold Set for Third Weekly Gain on US Treasury Buyback Plans

title: Negative Economic Surprises Could Help Treasuries, HSBC’s Kettner Says

title: Euro-Zone Business Activity Sees Surprise Improvement
summary: Private-sector activity in the euro area unexpectedly improved slightly in August, thanks to the strongest manufacturing growth in more than four years. Bloomberg's Zoe Schneeweiss reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: RBI Deputy Gupta Sounds Upbeat on Economy, Sees 7% Growth

title: Is Bessent Facing a Bond Market Credibility Issue?
summary: Jefferies Economist Modupe Adegbembo and Morgan Stanley Chief European Equity Strategist Marina Zavolock weigh the impact of US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's announcement that the department would at least double the size of its long-dated bond buybacks. They speak on Bloomberg Television. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Making Battlefield Tech Fuels an 80% Rally for Swedish Stock
summary: A small Swedish firm is Europe’s best-performing defense stock in 2026, an ascent its chief executive puts down to a “third wave” of military spending that’s focused more on computer systems and drones than tanks and ammunition.

title: IMO Contradicts Trump Claims on Strait of Hormuz
summary: IMO Secretary-General Arsenio Dominguez tells Bloomberg TV that the Strait of Hormuz is not open and that there is no confirmation that mines have been removed in the waterway, contradicting statements by US President Donald Trump. He says, "Until we have confirmation of demining and security that the vessels are not going to be attacked, I will not call for anyone in the area to take the risk to transit." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: What's Next Following Monte dei Paschi's High-Stakes Move?
summary:
Banca Monte dei Paschi is seeking to buy two separate banks for a combined price of €34 billion ($40 billion) in a defensive move designed to ward off a takeover by rival Intesa Sanpaolo.
The Italian lender said it’s launching an all-share bid for Banco BPM valuing it at €25.3 billion and another one for Banca Generali valuing it at €8.7 billion, based on the market close two days ago, according to a statement Friday. Bloomberg's Tommaso Ebhardt reports from Milan. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: India Allows Rare Tax-Free Sugar Imports to Cool Prices
